column2: req_desc

Hero arrival
Opening `/` plays the hero intro to its end. Any key, pointer press, wheel turn or scroll ends it at once, and `Explore projects` and `Start a project` land on their sections with focus on the heading and one new history entry.

Hero copy and intro timeline
The `intro` section shows the published hero copy and sculpture and carries `data-intro="playing"` and then `"done"` at the published moment. Each published intro motion plays at its published start and length, and the page opens in the done state with reduced motion, with a hash, or with a `category` or `service` parameter.

Copy drift
The hero copy moves up by the published share of the scroll position, capped as published. It returns exactly when the visitor scrolls back, and it stays put with reduced motion.

Sculpture tilt
Mouse or pen movement over the hero sets the sculpture's `data-tilt-x` and `data-tilt-y` and its rotation by the published formula, and both return to 0 when the pointer leaves. Touch, widths under 768 px and reduced motion keep both at 0.

Editorial look
The site reads as the published inked editorial sheet: pale sage paper, near-black ink bands for the hero and footer, one ultramarine accent, hairline rules, the three published typefaces and an asymmetric twelve-column grid.

Role line journey
A visitor watches the role line rotate, steps through roles by button and keyboard, and pauses and resumes the rotation. At every moment exactly one role shows, and its text matches its index.

Automatic role rotation
After the intro ends, the shown role advances on the published page-clock interval in the published order and wraps from 6 to 1. Each change's text and index are in place the moment the change starts.

Manual role changes and holds
`Next role` and `Previous role` change the role at once, counting from the incoming role during a slide, and restart the countdown. Hovering the line or focusing a role button holds the rotation, and the next automatic change comes one full interval after the hold ends.

Pausing and reduced-motion roles
`Pause roles` and `Play roles` stop and resume automatic changes with their published announcements, resuming with the next change one interval later while focus stays on the button. Screen readers read the roles summary instead of the line, and reduced motion starts paused with instant changes.

Scroll and jump journey
A visitor scrolls the home page down and back up while the current header link and the career journey follow. They jump between sections by header link and move back and forward through those jumps.

Current section marking
Exactly one header link carries `aria-current="true"` by the published 40% line rule, in both scroll directions. No link is current above `about` or on a case study, and the rule also holds without `IntersectionObserver` or `ResizeObserver`.

Career journey progress
Each milestone's `data-reached` and the progress `data-value` follow the published 60% line rule in the same moment as the scroll, in both directions. Each milestone button shows or hides its detail.

Section jump landing
Every section jump lands its heading 80 px from the viewport top, within 2 px, with focus on that heading. A jump by link glides and arrives within one second, a jump on load or with reduced motion is instant, and a second jump started during a glide wins.

Jump history
Each section jump by link adds one history entry with the target hash, and `Ottoline Rask home` and `Back to top` each add one without a hash. Back and Forward restore each entry's position, focus and current link instantly.

Keyboard-only tour
A keyboard-only visitor tabs through the whole home page, opens a milestone detail, and opens a case study from its card link by Enter. They arrive with the case study's title and focus on its level-1 heading.

Tab order and skip link
From a fresh load, the Tab order on `/` matches the published list at 1280x800 and the published start at 768x1024 and 375x812. `Skip to content` is the first stop; it is visible while focused and moves focus to the level-1 heading.

Visible, unhidden focus
Every focused control shows the published focus ring, and only while it is focused. Every focus change on an element in the page flow scrolls the page so it sits at least 8 px below the header, as qualified in Interactions.

Closed means unreachable
A closed menu, a collapsed or collapsing service panel, a closed milestone detail, a hidden skill panel and a hidden review slide expose nothing to Tab or to screen readers, at every published viewport.

Glyphs and new-tab links
The `→` and `↗` glyphs are visible but absent from accessible names, and `(opens in a new tab)` is in the name but not visible. Every new-tab link carries `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

Filter, read and return
A product lead presses several disciplines and opens a shown project's case study. They return by `Back to work` or the browser's Back to the same filters, cards and result line, with focus on that project's card link.

Discipline filtering
Toggling disciplines shows exactly the published matching cards in published order, and `All` is pressed exactly when no discipline is. The result line and its single announcement update in the same moment, without a reload.

Filter address
The pressed disciplines live in the `category` parameter in canonical order, and each change replaces the current history entry. An opened address with unknown or repeated values is applied and rewritten to canonical form at once.

Gallery return
Returning from a case study by `Back to work` or Back restores the list, the cards and the result line, with focus on that project's title link clear of the header and no announcement.

Case study reading
A visitor reads a case study with `On this page`, steps to neighbouring projects and goes back with the browser. Each arrival shows its title, with focus on its level-1 heading.

Case study content
Each `/work/<slug>` shows its title, kind, illustrative description list, the five published sections and the exact published stack list, under the published document title.

On this page
The current `On this page` link follows the published 40% line rule in both directions, and its links jump by the section jump rules.

Neighbour projects
`Previous project` and `Next project` link to the published neighbours within the address's `category` list and keep the parameter. Each is absent at its end of the list.

Not found and server boundary
Unknown pages answer 404 with the published not-found page. API routes answer in the published error order, and the server sends no CORS headers, cookies or Content-Security-Policy and never serves source files, source maps, `.env`, `run.json` or package files.

Preview and callout journey
A creative director reveals a card, steps through its quick-look frames by keyboard, opens the case study and ties each callout to its region and frame range. They recover a missing frame or a missing media library without a restart.

Card reveal and quick look
Cards carry `data-revealed` on hover and focus, and always below 768 px. The quick-look dialog opens on frame 1 with focus on `Next frame`, steps without wrapping, keeps Tab inside, and returns focus to its opener on close.

Callout Thread
Selecting a callout outlines its published region within 1 px, steps the frame through its published range on the page clock, shows the readout, announces the selection and keeps it in the address by replacement. Arrow keys, clearing, selection from the address and reduced motion behave as qualified in Interactions.

Media route and manifest
The 42 published objects are stored at their keys, and the browser receives them only through `GET /media/<key>` with the stored bytes and type. The route uses the published 404 and 503 bodies, and `GET /api/media` reports each object's availability.

Media fallback and recovery
A single missing object shows its fallback plate, and an unreachable library shows plates everywhere plus `Media notice`, while every page still works. Health reports `unavailable` only when storage cannot be reached or mail refuses a connection. Frames recover through `Try again`, and covers and the notice recover through the page's re-check, without a restart, as qualified in Business rules.

Service to enquiry
A founder opens a service panel, reads its deliverables and technology, and follows `Enquire about <service name>` to the form. The project type is chosen, focus is on `Your name`, and anything already typed is kept.

Service panels
Service panels open and close by click, Enter and Space with `aria-expanded`, and at most one is open. Each shows the exact published lists, and nothing in a closed or closing panel can be reached.

Enquire link prefill
Following an enquire link jumps to `contact` without a reload, sets `Project type` and moves focus to `Your name`. Every typed value is kept, the change is announced once, and one history entry is added.

Service parameter on load
Opening `/?service=<value>#contact` in a fresh page gives the prefilled state instantly. An unknown value is removed from the address and selects nothing.

Skills browsing
A visitor moves through the skill groups by keyboard, opens a technology card and follows a `Used in:` link to a case study.

Skill tabs
The `Skill groups` tabs select on focus with ArrowRight and ArrowLeft (wrapping), Home and End. They keep a single Tab stop and show only the selected panel.

Skill cards and meters
Each panel shows its four published cards, with meters carrying the published names and values from the moment the panel shows. A card's detail lists the published `Used in:` case studies or the published no-match text.

Skills layout and bars
The tabs and cards follow the published rows and columns at 1280, 768 and 375 wide. The bars grow with the published timing and stagger each time a panel shows, and appear at once with reduced motion.

Reading reviews
A founder on a phone swipes through the five illustrative reviews and back, and hears each new position announced once.

Review buttons and keys
`Previous review` and `Next review` move one review without wrapping and are disabled at the ends, with focus moving off a button that becomes disabled. ArrowRight, ArrowLeft, Home and End work with focus anywhere in the carousel.

Review swipe
A mostly horizontal touch or mouse drag of at least 40 px on the track moves one review when released. Shorter, mostly vertical or past-the-end movements change nothing.

Review exposure and announcements
Only the shown slide is exposed to screen readers and to Tab, and the position reads `<k> / 5`. Each change is announced once with the published text.

Counters on the way down
A visitor scrolls to `numbers`, scrolls away mid-count and comes back, and sees each figure finish exactly once at its target.

Counter start and figures
Each counter block starts at the published 75% line moment, also after a jump or a resize and without `IntersectionObserver`. It then shows the published floor figures on the page clock until its target at 1,500 ms.

Count once per load
Scrolling away and back, jumps, resizes and tab switches never restart, pause or reset a counter block. Only a reload starts it over.

Counter accessibility and reduced motion
Screen readers read each counter's label and final value from load. Reduced motion shows the targets with `data-state="done"` as soon as the block would start.

Enquiry delivered
A founder sends a valid enquiry and sees `Message received.` only after the mail server has accepted it. The studio inbox then holds exactly one email with every submitted field.

Enquiry validation
Sending an invalid form shows the published field messages, `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby` and the count in `Form status`, and moves focus to the first failing field. After the first send, every input is checked again in the same moment.

Sending and sent states
A valid press shows the published sending state, disables every field while keeping its value, and sends one request. A 201 replaces the form with the published sent panel, which stays until `Send another message` or a reload.

Enquiry API and email
`POST /api/enquiries` checks the published rules and sends exactly one email with the published recipient, sender, Reply-To, subject and body. It answers 201 only after the mail server accepted the message, and a line break in the name never reaches a mail header.

Mail outage and retry
When mail is unreachable or slow, the server answers the published 503. The form shows the published not-sent message with every value kept and focus on `Send message`, and the next press sends once mail is back, without a restart.

Phone visit
A founder on a phone opens the menu, jumps to a section and swipes the reviews, using touch and reduced motion. They meet the published phone layout throughout.

Mobile menu
Below 1024 px, `Menu` opens the modal `Menu` dialog with focus on `About` and Tab wrapping inside. Escape, `Close menu` or a tap outside closes it with focus back on `Menu`, and choosing a link closes it and jumps with focus on the target heading; reopening it mid-close keeps it open, and nothing inside is reachable while it is closed.

Published layouts and targets
At 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800, the header, hero, gallery, services, counters, contact and footer follow the published layouts with no horizontal overflow, and every target is at least 44 px at 375 wide. Every page has `lang="en"`, one `main` landmark, one level-1 heading and no automated accessibility violations.

Custom cursor and footer wordmark
The custom cursor follows the mouse within 1 px with the published states and hides on touch, pen, leaving the window and reduced motion. The footer wordmark plays its wave once per load and sets `data-waved`.

Credentials, media and motion source integrity
The source reads every credential and service address from the published environment variables, keeps object-store access on the server and generates its own artwork. It builds motion only on the browser's own animation features, with no animation library.
`/app/run.json` exists, is valid JSON with string fields `install`, `build` and `serve` and `"_schema":"run-manifest-v1"`, and its commands install, build and serve the site.

`/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` lists every shipped package and the three font families (Fraunces, IBM Plex Sans, IBM Plex Mono), each with its licence. Shipped packages means the production dependency tree reported by `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`.
Every shipped package uses the MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0 or 0BSD licence, and every font file uses the SIL Open Font License 1.1.
The site uses no datastore, broker, queue or service other than the provided mail server and media library, and no database, file-based ones included.
The shipped packages contain no animation library, and no page loads a font, script, style, image or video from another origin.
Every colour in the style sheets is written as a plain hexadecimal or red-green-blue value (alpha allowed), never as a colour-mixing or other colour function.
The provided service configuration and its development credentials stay unchanged.
All artwork is original and made for the site, and the covers and preview frames reach the media library only through the app's own storing at start or on recovery.
